trigger: ILC-EXP-001 added PMID 35663259 (CDH1-mutant 5yr PI3Ki CR) + PMID 35665642 (CDH1→IGF1R→PI3K second axis) + PMID 30332649 (CDH1+PIK3CA mouse ILC cooperation)
claim: CDH1 loss in ILC creates a DUAL PI3K hyperactivation axis conferring CDK4/6i resistance: (1) DIRECT: CDH1 loss disrupts E-cadherin/p85/p110alpha adherens junction complex → PI3Ka constitutive activation (Bahreini 2017); (2) INDIRECT: CDH1 loss releases negative regulation of IGF1R → IGF1R → PI3K/AKT amplification (Elangovan 2022). Both axes converge on AKT → CDK2/Cyclin E → RB1-independent G1/S bypass. Alpelisib (PI3Ka-selective) overcomes this dual resistance pattern. CDH1-mutant ILC patients who progressed on CDK4/6i should show superior alpelisib response vs IDC (CDH1-wildtype), supported by a clinical case of 5-year complete response in CDH1+PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer (PMID 35663259).
mechanistic_update: Prior versions described only the direct CDH1→PI3Ka mechanism (Bahreini 2017). ILC-EXP-001 identified an orthogonal IGF1R axis (Elangovan 2022): CDH1 loss releases E-cadherin's negative regulation of IGF1R, amplifying downstream PI3K/AKT. The two axes are additive and ILC-specific. Clinical case report (PMID 35663259) provides the first human evidence of exceptional PI3Ki response in CDH1-mutant breast cancer.
